messages:
Tara: @incident-bot paging — customer reports that usage dashboards are showing 0 for some accounts and yesterday's invoice run hasn't produced PDFs for multiple customers. Seeing spikes in support tickets. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: [pager] Severity: S2 — metering-display / invoice-generation anomaly detected. On-call: @Amy (SRE), @Mike. Pager started.
Amy (SRE): On it. I can see error traces in meter-aggregator logs — 'checkpoint corruption' around the 04:12 UTC window. Investigating if this affected the daily billing rollup.
Mike: I'm running a query to enumerate affected customers (by missing rollup rows) — should have an initial sample in ~8m.
Tara: Kate, hold on external comms until we confirm scope. I'll draft a status page + customer note here for review.
Kate (Support Lead): Copy. We have 4 escalations right now, one is enterprise with legal review. No public comms until we have confirmed impact and an ETA.
Amy (SRE): Quick root cause notes: aggregator checkpoint write failed due to transient NFS timeout on node agg-3. Checkpoint corruption caused the windowed compaction to skip a segment. Rolling restart of aggregator process mitigates immediate failure but backlog + missing compacted segments mean display lookups return empty for some time ranges. Invoice generation depends on the same compaction job so PDFs are queued.
Mike: Canary restart on shard agg-3 -> restarting now. If canary is good I'll roll restarts for agg-4 -> agg-7.
Amy (SRE): Canary stable. No duplicate billing rows detected in initial validation. Backfill job (meter-backfill) currently at ~620/s, queued ~12k. Estimated time to process queue ~20–25m at current rate; will scale if IO permits.
Tara: Draft statuspage update (short):
```
Service: Billing / Metering
Impact: Some customers may see delayed or zeroed usage in dashboards; invoices for the 04:00 UTC billing window are delayed.
Start: 2026-03-14 04:12 UTC
Status: Mitigation in progress — backfill processing underway; canary restarts successful.
ETA: 1–3 hours for display reconciliation; invoice generation to resume in parallel.
Notes: We do not expect double-billing. We will post an update once reconciliation completes and provide guidance for customers who need immediate export of raw usage.
```
Mike: Suggest adding 'no action required by customers' and a contact link for urgent escalations.
Tara: Added contact note and link. Draft customer email (support template):
```
Subject: Update — temporary delay in usage display and invoice generation
Hi {{first_name}},
We're reaching out because we detected an issue that may cause temporary delays in usage appearing in your dashboard and a short delay in invoice generation for the billing window that started 04:00 UTC on 2026-03-14. Our engineers have identified the root cause and are running backfill and reconciliation across affected accounts.
What this means for you:
- Dashboard may show 0 or stale usage for a short period.
- Invoices scheduled today may be delayed; once generated they will reflect correct usage.
What we're doing:
- Restarted affected aggregator nodes and started backfill processing.
- Validating data to ensure no duplicate charges.
ETA: Most accounts should be reconciled within 1–3 hours. If you need an immediate usage export or have a billing question, reply to this message or contact support@redwood.ai and we'll prioritize your request.
Apologies for the disruption — Tara, Billing
```
Kate (Support Lead): Ok to send to low-touch customers after next statuspage update. For enterprise accounts we need a tailored note and legal loop-in.
Rachel (Legal): Looping in — please do not commit to crediting or adjustments in the customer email. If enterprise requests compensation we'll coordinate case-by-case.
billing-bot: Billing workflow note: suspended invoice generation for run 04:00 until reconciliation flag cleared.
Amy (SRE): Live mitigation steps executed: restarted agg-3 canary -> rolled restarts agg-4..agg-7, kicked meter-backfill with concurrency bumped to 8, monitoring for duplicates with quick checksum predicate. No checksum mismatches so far.
Mike: Added temporary throttle to dashboard read path for affected time windows to prevent customers from seeing partial/empty state while backfill processes.
Tara: Support playbook (short):
- If customer asks: acknowledge, provide ETA from status page, offer usage export.
- If enterprise: escalate to Kate + Legal + Tara for a bespoke update.
- If customer reports double charges after resolution: open billing-recon ticket and tag Amy + Mike.
Kate (Support Lead): Creating a queue for affected customers and adding tags: urgent-enterprise, metering-delay.
Jonah: I'm coming on second-line for the night shift at 1891234625 — handoff notes: backfill in progress, current rate ~650/s, queued ~10.5k, monitoring log/error rate. Pager still active for regressions.
Mike: Thanks, Jonah. I've left the validation query and runbook in #eng-infra. Key commands:
```bash
# quick check for missing rollups
SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) FROM meter_rollups WHERE ts >= '2026-03-14T04:00:00Z' GROUP BY account_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 0 LIMIT 100;
# force backfill job
kubectl -n metering patch cronjob meter-backfill -p '{"spec":{"concurrencyPolicy":"Forbid"}}'
```
Amy (SRE): Monitoring dashboards to watch: backfill-queue-depth, aggregator-error-rate, invoice-generator-queue. Alerts set: invoice-generator-queue > 5k for >5m -> page S2.
Tara: Final check on customer comms: do not publish until we confirm invoices will not be re-run erroneously. Once billing-bot clears the 'hold' flag we'll post the statuspage and send the support template to non-enterprise customers.
billing-bot: Hold flag cleared at 1891234610 — invoice generation resumed in safe mode.
Tara: Posting statuspage now. Kate, you can start sending support-template to low-touch customers. Kate (Support Lead): Sending in batches, first batch sent to 120 customers.
Jonah: Handoff ack — I'll monitor through the night and escalate to Amy/Mike if queues grow or checksum mismatches appear.
Amy (SRE): Follow-up: full reconciliation completed at 1891234820. All queued backfills processed, invoice generation completed and PDFs delivered. No duplicated billing rows; one customer had an edge-case export mismatch that was corrected manually.
Tara: Closing notes for postmortem: include root cause (NFS transient causing checkpoint corruption), why checkpoint write didn't auto-recover, add redundancy to compaction pipeline, and a playbook to hold invoice runs until backfill finishes. Also include customer comms timeline and support queue impact.
Mike: Filing incident in postmortems with links to runbooks and the exact queries used.
Kate (Support Lead): Final: support queue drained, enterprise customers notified directly.
Tara: Thanks everyone — incident resolved. :white_check_mark:
